facts.text: Labeling, or annotation, is marking the contents of recorded sensor data so detectors can be trained and their results scored.
facts.quote: Labeling, or annotation, is the work of marking what is in recorded sensor data, such as drawing a box around each person and naming it, so that detectors can be trained and their results scored.

facts.text: Human labeling can handle any class, including workers in protective clothing and partially hidden people, but is slow and costly.
facts.quote: Human labeling handles any class, including workers in protective clothing and partially hidden people, but is slow and costly

facts.text: A major on-road study found human labels less consistent than expected.
facts.quote: a major on-road study found human labels less consistent than expected.

facts.text: Automatic or offboard labeling uses large models that can examine the whole recording, including past and future frames together.
facts.quote: Automatic or offboard labeling uses large models that can look at the whole recording, past and future frames together

facts.text: On-road studies report automatic or offboard labels matching or beating average human labels for lidar boxes on vehicles.
facts.quote: on-road studies report such labels matching or beating average human labels for lidar boxes on vehicles

facts.text: Automatic or offboard labelers need human-labeled data to begin with and inherit the conditions they were trained on.
facts.quote: they need human-labeled data to begin with, inherit the conditions they were trained on

facts.text: One 2026 general-purpose labeler reached recall of 0.88 to 0.98 but precision of only 0.52 in crowded scenes.
facts.quote: one 2026 general-purpose labeler reached recall of 0.88 to 0.98 but precision of only 0.52 in crowded scenes.

facts.text: No automatic or offboard labeler described in the passage has been validated for workers and machines near heavy equipment.
facts.quote: None has been validated for workers and machines near heavy equipment.

facts.text: A label specification should define the object taxonomy, object reference points, visibility and occlusion state, whether a partially hidden person counts as a detection opportunity, temporal continuity rules, and disagreement resolution.
facts.quote: A label specification should define the object taxonomy, the reference point on each object, visibility and occlusion state, whether a partially hidden person counts as a detection opportunity, rules for continuity over time, and how disagreements are settled

facts.text: Where distance matters, labels should rest on calibrated three-dimensional reference data.
facts.quote: where distance matters, labels should rest on calibrated three-dimensional reference data

facts.text: Labeling cost figures for off-road work were not found; the booklet recommends a small annotation trial to estimate those costs.
facts.quote: Labeling cost figures for off-road work were not found; a small annotation trial is the right way to estimate them

facts.text: A labeler missing distant workers inflates the apparent false-alarm rate, while label position errors shift the measured warning distance.
facts.quote: a labeler who misses distant workers inflates the apparent false-alarm rate, and position errors shift the measured warning distance

facts.text: The booklet recommends measuring label precision and recall on an audited subset and reporting them with every result.
